newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban says it has reached key Afghan tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Taleban says it has reached key Afghan tunnel.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic movement said on Tuesday its forces had reached the southern mouth of the strategic Salang tunnel north of Kabul, where they had been stopped by the forces of a powerful northern warlord.
The Taleban forces reached the mouth of the tunnel on Tuesday afternoon, the official Kabul Radio, monitored in Islamabad, said. "So far nothing has happened there," it said.

On Monday General Rashid Dostum's forces had advanced several km (miles) south of the tunnel to a position about three km (two miles) from those of Taleban after refusing their demand for a passage to the north. The move sparked fears of a confrontation between the two forces.

The area south of the tunnel was previously occupied by forces loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani, whose government was ousted from Kabul on Friday when Taleban captured the capital without a fight.

It was not immediately clear whether Taleban was seeking passage through the famous Soviet-built tunnel to attack some northern provinces still held by pro-Rabbani forces or wanted to capture Dostum's territory.

Dostum has so far stayed out of the fighting between Taleban and the former Kabul government, which he also opposed. A spokesman for Dostum in the northern town of Mazar-i-Sharif said on Tuesday his forces wanted to negotiate with Taleban.
